question_text: Find the condition for the line lx + my + n = 0 to be a tangent to the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1.

mark_split.label: Write the tangent at the parametric point

insider_note: This condition a²l² + b²m² = n² specialises to the familiar y = mx ± √(a²m² + b²) formula when the line is written as y = mx − c (l = m-value, m-coefficient = −1, n = −c) — recognising that connection is a useful cross-check, not a separate derivation.

steps.label: Write the tangent at the parametric point
steps.margin_note: First mark. Every point on the ellipse can be written as (a cos θ, b sin θ) for some angle θ.
steps.memory_tip: The parametric point on x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 is always (a cos θ, b sin θ).
lines: Let lx + my + n = 0 be the tangent
at the point P(θ) = (a cos θ, b sin θ)

steps.why: Writing the tangent at the general parametric point P(θ) lets the given line lx + my + n = 0 be matched against it directly, since a tangent line at ANY point on the ellipse has this same form.
common_mistakes: Writing the parametric point as (a sin θ, b cos θ) with sin and cos swapped.
Using the S₁ = 0 tangent formula with (x₁, y₁) instead of the θ-form, which makes the comparison step below harder.

steps.label: Compare with the given line
steps.margin_note: Middle two marks. Match the tangent's coefficients to l, m, n, up to a common ratio.
steps.memory_tip: Two lines represent the same line exactly when their coefficients of x, y and the constant are all in the same ratio.

steps.why: Since both equations describe the same line, their x-coefficients, y-coefficients and constants must all be in one common ratio — that ratio is set equal to −1/n by comparing the constant terms.
common_mistakes: Comparing lx + my + n = 0 with the tangent written as = 1 without first moving n to match the −1 form, causing a sign slip.
Losing the a and b when isolating cos θ and sin θ.

steps.label: Apply the identity and conclude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 turns the two expressions above into the final condition.
steps.memory_tip: Whenever cos θ and sin θ are both isolated, squaring and adding using cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 is the natural next step.

lines.text: This is the condition for lx + my + n = 0

steps.why: Since cos θ and sin θ must satisfy cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 for every angle θ, substituting the expressions found in step 2 gives the condition that l, m, n must satisfy for the line to be a tangent.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to square both al/n and bm/n before adding.
Writing the final condition with n on the wrong side, e.g. a²l² + b²m² + n² = 0.
